cost: THE RULING'S NUMBER IS 79 AND THE SUBJECT LANDS 81 — inside the dispatch's 79 +-3 and NOT on its centre, and the frontier is stated rather than hidden. The wall is recal_126's ORDER pin (John Stockton '97 >= John Stockton '01) standing over recal_176's John Stockton '01 86 +-2. '97 is volume 23 with a 19.84 passer term and '01 is volume 31 with 15.25, so every load condition on this term costs '97 MORE than '01 and '97's whole cushion is 1.81 of raw. MEASURED on the full pipeline: PD_E_V_FULL 30 prints subject 81, '97 86, '01 86 (the pin holds, level); 32 — the same quartile taken on recal_176's WIDER playvol >= 70 class — prints subject 81, '97 85, '01 86 and FAILS the pin; 46 prints the subject at 79 EXACTLY, '97 83 and '01 84 and fails it by a point. A ramp that reaches 79 with the pin held would need its foot at the subject's own volume, which is a name in disguise.

JOHN STOCKTON '97 AND '01 ARE NOW LEVEL AT 86, where they were 88 and 86. data/anchors.py grades an order pin `>=` by its own written definition, so the pin passes, but a later round should know the pair is now TIED and has no slack left: any further dock on this term, from any direction, inverts them. That is the single largest cost of this round.

FIVE STOCKTON SEASONS AND FOUR CALDERÓNS MOVE TOGETHER, and that is the round working rather than a side effect: '88 81 -> 75, '96 89 -> 86, '95 88 -> 86, '97 88 -> 86, '94 84 -> 82, '89 85 -> 84, '98 83 -> 82, '87 62 -> 57, '86 55 -> 52 — the seasons where he carried 15-23% of the offence, never the ones where he carried more. Calderón '13 79 -> 76, '12 73 -> 70, '10 71 -> 70, '08 82 -> 81. Maurice Cheeks '82 67 -> 61 and Terry Porter '88 71 -> 68 are the same card type. None of the nine is pinned.

OFF_TOP AND DEF_TOP WERE NOT RE-DERIVED (recal_90's warning): the band anchors are untouched at 102.75 / 104.25, nothing above the knee was rescaled, the top 12 by OFF is identical and the summit order is unchanged. DEF moved on ZERO cards — this round is entirely inside one factor of one term of o_score.

THE HUNT TAX WAS RE-SWEPT ONCE from main's constants (hunt 4.22 / crashOff 0.28 / crashDef 0.66) and moved 4.22 -> 3.92, the mirror of recal_176's move in the same knob. crashOff and crashDef held. See the knob line and the comment block in src/engine/tactics.ts.

The two remaining levers are the playvol foot PD_PV_LO 70, which recal_112's `playvol <= 70` gate holds disjoint, and a new channel. Nothing in the fitted direction has slack.
notes: THE SUBJECT, DECOMPOSED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS TOUCHED. José Calderón '09: 12.8 points, 8.9 assists, 34.3 minutes, usg 17.1, TS .603, BPM 2.8, volume 19. Of an o_score of 90.91 this term was 19.65 — gate 0.89 x eff factor 1.00 x load 0.988, about 18 printed points, against 71.26 without it. The gate is recal_117's and it is right. The FACTOR was the defect: a .603 conversion mark taken on 17.1% of his team's possessions was paid the same 1.00 lift as a creator converting at that rate while carrying a fifth of the offence. recal_96 settled exactly this for the standard path and recal_130 for this term's second payment of minutes; the conversion factor was the last rate on the card paid at full price on no load at all. The term now reads gate 0.89 x eff factor 0.82 (lift 1.00 x scoring load 0.63) x load 0.988 = +16.05, and he prints 81.

WHY THE LIFT AND NOT THE TERM, AND IT IS A PROOF RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. Mark Jackson '98 is pinned 55 +-3, reads 52 (raw 52.411) and can lose 0.98 of o_score — 9.9% of his 9.93 term. The subject must lose 30% of his. Jackson's volume is 12 and the subject's is 19, so no factor MONOTONE AND RISING in scoring load can dock 19 by three times what it docks 12: a load condition on the whole term is infeasible before a constant is chosen, the same shape recal_82 and recal_130 recorded. Scaling the LIFT ABOVE THE FLOOR moves the whole bottom of the class out of the way at once — 592 of the 1,235 cards the term pays have efficiency at or under the ramp's foot and are byte-identical by arithmetic, Mark Jackson '98 and '99 among them.

WHY THE LOWER QUARTILE AND NOT THE MEDIAN, MEASURED ON THE FULL PIPELINE EACH TIME. The class's own median volume is 52 and it prints the subject at 79 — his number, read off the full pipeline — while printing John Stockton '01 at 83 against a pin of 86 +-2 and John Stockton '97 at 83 with him. p25 = 30.0 is the deepest cut in this family that holds every standing pin, and it is a MEASURED quantile of the class the term pays rather than a fitted value: 25th percentile 30.0 under linear, nearest-rank and lower-interpolation conventions alike (p10 16, p20 26, p50 52, p75 74). The knee it puts in the term is small and honest — a distributor carrying less scoring than the bottom quarter of his own class is paid his conversion percentile pro rata, and everyone else is paid exactly what recal_176 paid him.

THE FOOTPRINT. 58 cards move on OFF, EVERY ONE DOWN, largest fall 6 (John Stockton '88 81 -> 75); 48 move on OVR, max 4; ZERO move on DEF. Rank flips touching the top 50 by OVR: none. Four of the 150 campaign levels change a single player's card and no five changes membership (Celtics '81, 76ers '83, All-time Jazz, All-Hall-of-Fame). ANCHORS: 178 pins, 0 failing, mean |error| 0.80 — identical to main's 0.80 on the same measure.

WHAT WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED. (1) A load factor on the WHOLE term — infeasible against Mark Jackson '98 before a constant is chosen, shown above. (2) Load-scaling the efficiency INPUT (`efficiency x min(1, volume/H)`, walking the man down recal_176's ramp instead of scaling his lift) — decomposed on the two cards rather than run: at H = 52 the subject's efficiency 87 reads as 31.8, BELOW the ramp's foot of 43, so his factor drops to the bare 0.5 floor (o_score -9.83, off 75, under his own tolerance) while John Stockton '01's 97 reads as 57.8 and costs him four points he does not have. The ramp's foot is a cliff for anyone the load pushes through it, which is exactly what the multiplicative form on the lift avoids. (3) The same lift ramp on the load-scaled `_vol` (volume x recal_96's load share) — every card in this class is over the 24-minute full-load line, so it is the same number with more arithmetic. (4) PD_E_V_FULL at 32 (the wider playvol >= 70 class's p25) and at 46 (the value that lands the subject on 79 exactly) — both break recal_126's order pin, and 32 does not even move the subject.
